name: Four Rooted Inputs Robust to Deleting Short Geodesic Paths
definition: From the normalized 289-concept rooted core $C$, take the four ample families $C$, $C\cup\{290\}$, $C\cup\{128,160\}$, and $C\cup\{290,128,160\}$.
parameters: The numbers of unoriented four-vertex geodesic paths are respectively $13{,}368$, $13{,}480$, $13{,}561$, and $13{,}675$.
properties: For every geodesic path on one through four vertices in each family, deleting the path leaves a nonempty connected graph. Consequently, even after attaching arbitrary finite trees on fresh disjoint coordinate blocks, these inputs cannot support a four-vertex-path expansion with two attainable lifts whose edge is not retainable.
